q-47028.name: Question 1
q-47028.worked_solution:
Let $f(x)=\sqrt[3]{x}.$ Let's sketch the graph of $y=f(x):$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14267961/assets/35cd7d1487285bcb2094325ab052a2a2eb13dfe8191ec125118387bc9d7a93d5.png)

From the graph, we see that the function increases without bound as $x$ increases. Therefore,

$$
{lim}_{x\to \infty }f(x)=\infty .
$$

q-47032.name: Question 2
q-47032.worked_solution:
We substitute $x=-2$ into the expression, and get

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to (-2)}\sqrt[3]{{x}^{2}-2x} & =\sqrt[3]{(-2)^{2}-2(-2)} \\  & =\sqrt[3]{8} \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$
